idea: When to replace old plumbing pipes
title: Identifying Internal Pipe Corrosion for Replacement
description: Low water pressure is not always caused by a clogged aerator or main supply drop. In older installations with galvanized steel water lines, oxygen and dissolved minerals react with the metal over time, causing internal rust buildup known as tuberculation. These rough iron oxide deposits accumulate inside the pipe, drastically narrowing the inner flow diameter while weakening the pipe wall from the inside out. Because this deterioration happens internally, an old pipe may look intact on the exterior while offering severely degraded performance. When flow capacity is choked by internal scale, full replacement with modern piping materials is required.
image_prompt: A macro technical photograph of a cutaway section of an old 3/4-inch galvanized steel water pipe, displayed vertically in a 9:16 aspect ratio. The cross-section clearly reveals severe internal tuberculation with heavy, crusty reddish-brown rust nodules and mineral scale chokepoints reducing the internal water flow opening to a fraction of its original size. The cut edges of the pipe show realistic metal grain and wall thickness. The pipe rests on a neutral grey workbench in a brightly lit professional workshop environment with soft directional lighting to emphasize the rough texture of the rust buildup inside the pipe. Photorealistic texture, sharp focus on the internal pipe chamber, clean visual space around the subject, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no artificial annotations.
visual_story: The visual presents a clear cross-sectional cutaway of an aging metal water pipe. The viewer immediately notices that while the outer surface appears solid, the internal waterway is nearly blocked by jagged, crusty rust deposits (tuberculation). This directly demonstrates why visual inspection of external pipe surfaces alone is insufficient to evaluate old plumbing supply lines.

on_image_text.hook: Pipes corrode from the inside out.
on_image_text.explanation: Internal rust nodules (tuberculation) choke water volume long before external leaks appear.
on_image_text.takeaway: Persistent multi-fixture pressure drops signal it is time to replace aging metallic lines.
